name: VARoleSecretaryExperimentPlanning1on1

custom.system_prompt: Dmitri and Rui plan the next round of experiments for Rui's project. Dmitri invites Sigma to keep track of the plan. They agree Rui should run a new ablation, but don't settle on which compute resources to use or by when. Sigma asks a small clarifying question about that.

initial_prompt: Generate a one-on-one planning meeting where Dmitri helps Rui plan the next round of experiments for his project. Dmitri invites Sigma to keep track of the plan at the start. They discuss recent results and agree Rui should run a new ablation study, normally, Sigma silent. They agree on the ablation but don't settle on which compute cluster to use or a target date. Sigma asks a small clarifying question about that. Keep every line short and natural.

user1.name: Dmitri
user1.tts_prompt: Measured, mentoring, asks questions rather than giving answers

variations.context: One-on-one experiment planning meeting ending with a vague resourcing/timing commitment

setting.relationship_dynamic: Senior researcher and PhD student working through next research steps together
setting.background: Recent results are promising but raise a question the team hasn't isolated via an ablation yet
setting.conversation_style: Natural one-on-one technical conversation, short lines

scenario_template.topic: Dmitri invites Sigma to keep track of the plan from this experiment planning session, addressing Sigma directly in one short line.
scenario_template.note: e.g. 'Sigma, keep track of the plan we land on.' Only explicit invocation.

scenario_template.topic: Dmitri asks Rui probing questions about the recent results, and together they identify that an ablation study is needed to isolate the cause, Sigma silent.
scenario_template.note: Dmitri's Socratic mentoring style, ordinary technical discussion.

scenario_template.topic: Rui agrees to run the ablation study, Dmitri agrees that's the right next step, but neither specifies which compute resources to use or a target completion date.
scenario_template.note: This is exactly the incomplete commitment Sigma should catch.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma asks a small, single clarifying question about which compute resources Rui will use and roughly when the ablation will be done.
scenario_template.note: e.g. 'Which cluster, and roughly when will that be done?' One short question only.

scenario_template.topic: Rui says he'll use the shared GPU cluster and expects results by early next week, Dmitri agrees that's reasonable, and they move to a smaller point, Sigma silent again.
scenario_template.note: Rui sets his own resourcing and timeline.

scenario_template.topic: Dmitri wraps the session and Sigma gives a brief summary of the ablation plan, the resources, and the target date.

user1.name: Dmitri
user1.role: Senior researcher, mentors by asking questions rather than giving direct answers, invites Sigma to track decisions. Speaks in short sentences.

user2.name: Rui
user2.role: Focused, somewhat reserved PhD student, proposes his own resourcing and timeline once asked. Speaks in short, technical sentences.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Secretary. Invited once at the start, stays silent through the technical discussion, and asks one small clarifying question only when the ablation commitment lacks resources and a date. Gives a brief end-of-meeting summary. Does not weigh in on the experimental design.

conversation_structure: Sigma is invited explicitly only once, at the start
Sigma stays silent through the technical discussion
Sigma speaks only to ask one small clarifying question when the ablation commitment lacks resources and a target date
Every line is short and natural
The meeting ends with a brief Sigma summary of the plan
assistant_behavior: Sigma does not weigh in on the experimental design
The two people decide everything; Sigma only remembers
